story.story:
The opening eight seconds show AA-1, the first prototype F-35A Lightning II, accelerating along the runway at Lockheed Martin’s Fort Worth, Texas, facility at 12:44 p.m. CST on December 15, 2006. The gray aircraft lifts off, its nose probe projecting forward and landing gear extended. “F-35A Lightning II” appears as it becomes airborne. “One engine” and then “Conventional takeoff” appear in turn while a calm English narrator says, “The F-35A has one engine. It uses conventional takeoff.”

Through the next twelve seconds, the film follows chief test pilot Jon Beesley flying AA-1 with its gear still down. A caption records 15,000 feet and 225 knots as he tests the aircraft in landing configuration, before continuing maneuvers evaluating aircraft handling, the engine and subsystems.

The final ten seconds move forward to AA-1’s landing. Its extended wheels meet the runway, and a closing caption gives the time: 1:19 p.m. CST, completing the inaugural flight 35 minutes after takeoff.
